region: TTR and modern type theories: scoped comparisons
summary: Existence of a stratified system of types satisfying the witness conditions of Cooper's Appendix A for basic types, ptypes, function types, dependent function types, singleton, join and meet types, Type^n, records, record types, dependent record types and manifest fields. The source states each construct as a condition on a given system; this file builds one system and proves it meets them together. Types and witness sets are defined together: ty c P says that the object c is a type whose witnesses are the objects satisfying P, which gives function types their real clause without a negative occurrence. Orders are built by recursion, each seeing the one below. Proved: one witness set per type, the clauses as biconditionals, cumulativity, no Type^k a witness of itself, independence of the order in which fields were added, and that a function type from an inhabited type into an empty one has no witness. A concrete system shows the conditions can be met.

sources.citation: Cooper, R. (2023). From Perception to Communication. OUP.
sources.available: Appendix A1-A11.2 (pp. 398-410) and section 1.4.3.2 read; A5, A9, A11.3-A13 read or skimmed and not formalized; chapters 2-8 not read for this file

theorems.name: one_witness_set
theorems.source_claim: S1. At every order a type has exactly one witness set. Not stated in the source; needed for the biconditional clauses of Appendix A to define the witness relation.

theorems.name: A2_basic_types
theorems.source_claim: S2. [C23 A2.1 clause 4, p. 400]: a : T iff a is in A(T).

theorems.name: A3_ptypes
theorems.source_claim: S2. [C23 A3.2 clauses 5 and 8, p. 401]: P(a1,...,an) is a ptype iff the arguments witness an arity of P; its witnesses are F(P(a1,...,an)).

theorems.name: A4_function_types
theorems.source_claim: S2. [C23 A4 clauses 1-2, p. 401]: f : (T1 -> T2) iff f is a function whose domain is the witnesses of T1 and whose range is included in the witnesses of T2. Functions are those of the model (difference D3).

theorems.name: A6_singleton_types
theorems.source_claim: S2. [C23 A6 clauses 1-2, pp. 403-404]: b : T_a iff b : T and a = b.

theorems.name: A7_A8_join_meet_types
theorems.source_claim: S2. [C23 A7, A8, p. 404]: binary join and meet types.

theorems.name: A10_stratification
theorems.source_claim: S3. [C23 A10 clauses 2, 4, 5, p. 406]: Type^n is included in Type^(n+1); Type^n is in Type^n for n > 0; T : Type^n iff T is in Type^(n-1). Also: no Type^k is a witness of itself.

theorems.name: A10_dependent_function_types
theorems.source_claim: S4. [C23 A10, dependent function types, clauses 1-2, p. 406].

theorems.name: A11_record_types
theorems.source_claim: S5. [C23 A11.2 clauses 1-8 and the intensional clauses 2-3, p. 409]: Rec, ERec, adding a plain field, RecType^n. The typedness condition of A11.1 is not imposed (difference D1).

theorems.name: A11_dependent_record_types
theorems.source_claim: S6. [C23 A11.2, dependent record types, clauses 1-2, pp. 409-410]: r witnesses R with the field <l, <F, <pi1,...,pim>>> iff r : R, r.pi_i : T_i, and r.l : F(r.pi1)...(r.pim).

theorems.name: record_type_witness
theorems.source_claim: S7. A record witnesses a record type iff it is a record and meets the condition of each field. Not stated in the source in this form.

theorems.name: order_independent
theorems.source_claim: S7. Two orders of adding the same fields give the same witnesses. Not stated in the source; its definition by decomposing R u {field} needs it.

theorems.name: manifest_field
theorems.source_claim: S8. [C23 A11.2, p. 410]: the manifest field [l=a : T] is the field <l, T_a>; it is witnessed exactly by records with r.l = a.

theorems.name: consistency
theorems.source_claim: S8. An empty type exists at every order; (T -> empty) has no witness when T has one and has the empty function as witness when T has none. Not stated in the source.

theorems.name: example_dependent_record_type
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity: in a concrete system, [x : Ind, c : dog(x)] is a type with one record that witnesses it and one that does not.

theorems.name: example_function_types
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity: (Ind -> Ind) has a witness and (Ind -> Nothing) has none.

theorems.name: example_manifest_field
theorems.source_claim: Non-vacuity: a manifest field in the concrete system.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.

D1. A11.1 requires every value in a record to be of some type. This is not imposed: a record is a finite labelled set with distinct labels. The condition makes Rec refer to all types of the system; whether a system with it exists is not settled here.
D2. Partial function types (A4), set and plurality types (A5), generalized joins and meets, modal systems (A9), merges and A11.3-A11.8, list and string types (A12, A13) are not modelled.
D3. Functions are abstract names with an application map. A function type contains the functions of the right domain and range that exist in the model, not all set-theoretic functions.
D4. Types are built with constructors, not as labelled sets with reserved labels. Records and record types are lists; order_independent shows field order does not affect witnesses.
D5. The assignments A and F do not vary with the order and are not required to be disjoint from the types.
D6. Rec is the record type with no fields.
The result is the existence of one system, relative to the consistency of Rocq. It is not a normalisation result: the source has no reduction relation.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The clauses transpose as biconditionals once types and witness sets are defined together; the typedness condition on records (A11.1) is dropped and is the main open point.

artifact_classes.description: witness sets as predicates on one value type; functions as names with an application map; types as constructors; records as lists

notes: Standalone; standard library only. It does not import TTR.v, which covers a first-order fragment (basic types, ptypes, meet, record types) with subtyping and merge and leaves out function types and stratification. Not yet cross-reviewed. No survey entry is linked to this file. DRAFT RECORD: the faithfulness verdict, the determination and the assessment status are the author's to set.
